description: The Application Architecture standard as checkable rules. rig runs the static and trace checks deterministically; the Reviewer's architecture lens is generated from the lens asks of the rules whose applies_when matches the unit's features.v1 structure.touches. A check at stage 'specified' is not yet run by rig; its rule still feeds the lens.

parameters.ownership_registry: Each service's data_stores list in its Genesis vending record; rig reads the vendored copy.

platform_spans.db.transaction: Wraps one database transaction, from begin to commit or rollback. Every db, client, and producer span inside it is its descendant.
platform_spans.outbox.relay: Root of the relay's trace: reads outbox rows and publishes them.
platform_spans.inbox.check: The consumer's lookup and insert of the event ID in its inbox table.

platform_attributes.app.timeout_ms: On every CLIENT span: the timeout configured for the call, in milliseconds; 0 when none is set. On a SERVER span: the request's deadline.
platform_attributes.app.retry.attempt: On every CLIENT span: 0 for the first attempt, then 1, 2, ...
platform_attributes.app.idempotency_key.present: On every non-idempotent CLIENT span: true when the request carries an idempotency key.
platform_attributes.app.db.isolation_level: On db.transaction: the isolation level the code chose.
platform_attributes.app.governor.limit: On spans run under a Governor: its configured concurrency limit.

rules.title: Modules import only each other's public interface
rules.intent: Module boundaries inside the monolith hold like repository boundaries, so a module can later become a service.

static_check.detects: An import of a path inside another module that is not in that module's declared public interface (rig rule illegal_boundary_import).

lens.ask: Does the change couple to another module's internal behavior through a side channel the import check cannot see (shared globals, reflection, string-keyed lookups)?

rules.title: A module becomes a service only for a recorded, measured reason
rules.intent: Each service adds a network hop, a failure mode, a pipeline, and an identity; it must pay for itself.

static_check.detects: A change adds a deployable unit without a split record naming the reason (scaling, failure isolation, ownership, runtime or security boundary) and its evidence.

lens.ask: Does the recorded evidence (RED/USE metrics, an incident record, an ownership conflict) actually support the split, or is the reason speculative?

rules.title: One owner per data store
rules.intent: Only the owning service reads or writes its store, so the owner can change its schema safely.

static_check.detects: IaC that grants a non-owner identity access to a store, or code and configuration in one service that connect to a store the ownership registry assigns to another.

trace_check.detects: A db span whose service.name is not the registered owner of its db.namespace.

lens.ask: Does the change read another service's data indirectly, for example through a shared reporting replica or an export file, instead of its API or events?

rules.title: Data crosses boundaries only through versioned contracts
rules.intent: APIs and events are the only interfaces between owners; contracts shared across repositories live once in schemas/.

static_check.detects: A cross-boundary payload type without a version, or a local copy of a contract that exists in the vendored schemas (rig rule contract_copy).

lens.ask: Does the change pass data between services through a channel that is not a versioned API or event?

rules.title: No network call inside a database transaction
rules.intent: A slow remote call holding a transaction open exhausts connection pools and locks.

static_check.detects: An HTTP, gRPC, or queue client call lexically inside a transaction callback or between begin and commit.

trace_check.detects: A span of kind CLIENT or PRODUCER that is a descendant of a db.transaction span, other than the transaction's own db spans.

lens.ask: Can any call inside the transaction block on something remote through indirection the checks did not exercise (a callback, an injected dependency, a lazy-loaded client)?

rules.title: Isolation level is chosen and recorded
rules.intent: The database default is a decision too; read-then-write workflows state theirs.

static_check.detects: A transaction that reads and then writes without an explicit isolation level.

trace_check.detects: A db.transaction span containing both read and write db operations with no app.db.isolation_level.

lens.ask: Is the chosen isolation level sufficient for this read-then-write workflow, or can a concurrent writer cause a lost update or a write skew?

rules.title: Connection pools are bounded Governors
rules.intent: A pool has a maximum size from Little's Law, a wait timeout, and metrics.

static_check.detects: A connection pool configured without a maximum size or an acquire timeout.

lens.ask: Is the pool size consistent with the expected arrival rate times P99 query duration, and with the database's connection limit across all replicas?

rules.title: One expand-or-contract step per change
rules.intent: Never break readers and writers in one step; each schema step deploys and reverts on its own.

static_check.detects: A migration that both adds and removes schema objects, renames a column or table in place, changes a column's type in place, or adds a NOT NULL column without a default.

lens.ask: Does the code in this change still work against both the previous and the next schema step?

rules.title: The contract step is irreversible and human-approved
rules.intent: Dropping the old shape cannot be undone; a person approves it after confirming a backup exists.

static_check.detects: A migration that drops a column, table, or index, or narrows a type. The hit routes the change to required human approval; it does not block by itself.

lens.ask: Has the switch-reads step run cleanly in production, and is anything still reading or writing the old shape?

rules.title: Backfills run in bounded, resumable batches
rules.intent: A backfill respects the Governor and can resume after a failure.

static_check.detects: A data migration that updates rows without a batch bound or a resume key.

lens.ask: Can the backfill be stopped and resumed without redoing or skipping rows, and does its rate stay under the database's headroom?

rules.title: Events are published through a transactional outbox
rules.intent: The business change and its event commit together; a relay publishes the event.

static_check.detects: A queue publish call in the same code path as a database commit, outside the outbox relay.

trace_check.detects: A PRODUCER span (messaging.operation.type publish or send) with no outbox.relay span among its ancestors. A broken ancestor chain is unverifiable.

lens.ask: Is every event this change emits written in the same transaction as the state change it announces?

rules.title: Consumers deduplicate through an inbox
rules.intent: A redelivered event changes nothing; consumers are safe to replay.

static_check.detects: A message handler that writes to the database without recording the event ID in an inbox table.

trace_check.detects: A CONSUMER process span with db write spans but no inbox.check span inside the same db.transaction.

lens.ask: Does the handler have side effects outside its database (emails, payments, third-party calls) that the inbox cannot make idempotent?

rules.title: Multi-service workflows are sagas, never distributed transactions
rules.intent: Each step commits locally and has a compensating action; two-phase commit is not used.

static_check.detects: Use of an XA or two-phase-commit API, or a transaction manager spanning more than one data store.

lens.ask: Does each step of the workflow have a compensating action, and is the workflow correct if a later step fails after earlier steps committed?

rules.title: Every queue declares delivery, ordering, and dead-lettering
rules.intent: Ordering is stated, poison messages go to a DLQ after bounded retries, and DLQ growth is a ticket.

static_check.detects: A queue or topic in IaC without a dead-letter target and a bounded maximum delivery attempts, or without documented ordering (none, or the ordering key).

lens.ask: Does the chosen ordering key match the consumer's ordering assumptions, and is the consumer correct when messages arrive out of order?

rules.title: Trace context crosses the queue
rules.intent: Producers put trace context in message headers, so one trace follows the message.

static_check.detects: A publish that bypasses the shared wrapper and does not inject trace context into message headers.

trace_check.detects: A CONSUMER process span with neither a parent nor a span link to a PRODUCER span (an orphaned trace).

lens.ask: Is trace context lost anywhere the message is transformed, batched, or re-published?

rules.title: Consumers pull through a Governor
rules.intent: A slow consumer lags; it does not fall over.

static_check.detects: A consumer subscription without a maximum concurrency or flow-control limit.

trace_check.detects: More concurrently open CONSUMER process spans for one subscription than its app.governor.limit.

lens.ask: What happens downstream of this consumer when the backlog is large: does the limit protect the database and the services it calls?

rules.title: Every remote call has a timeout shorter than the caller's deadline
rules.intent: A slow dependency cannot hold the caller.

static_check.detects: An HTTP or gRPC client created or called without a timeout.

trace_check.detects: A non-database CLIENT span whose app.timeout_ms is 0 (no timeout), that outlasted its app.timeout_ms by more than 50 ms, or whose app.timeout_ms is not shorter than its nearest ancestor's. A span without app.timeout_ms is unverifiable; the static check catches clients built without a timeout.

lens.ask: Do the timeouts on this path add up to less than the end-to-end deadline, including retries?

rules.title: Retries only for idempotent operations; writes carry idempotency keys
rules.intent: A retried request is applied once.

static_check.detects: A retry wrapper around a non-idempotent call (POST, PATCH) that sends no idempotency key, or a retry without backoff and jitter.

trace_check.detects: A CLIENT span with app.retry.attempt above 0, a non-idempotent http.request.method, and app.idempotency_key.present not true.

lens.ask: Does the server side honor the idempotency key, and does the retry budget stop a retry storm?

rules.title: Every list endpoint paginates
rules.intent: No unbounded responses.

static_check.detects: A route that returns a collection without a page size limit and a cursor or offset parameter.

lens.ask: Is the maximum page size enforced on the server, and is the cursor stable under concurrent inserts?

rules.title: Synchronous call chains stay shallow and acyclic
rules.intent: Long or circular synchronous chains between services are a distributed monolith.

trace_check.detects: A chain of synchronous CLIENT-to-SERVER hops across distinct service.name values deeper than max_sync_call_depth, or any service appearing twice on one chain.

lens.ask: Should part of this chain be an event instead of a synchronous call, or should the services be one module?

rules.title: Every cached item has a TTL and an invalidation path
rules.intent: Cache-aside by default; nothing is cached forever.

static_check.detects: A cache write without a TTL.

lens.ask: When the source data changes, what invalidates this entry, and how stale can a reader see it?

rules.title: Authorization decisions are never cached beyond their credential or shared
rules.intent: A cached authorization outlives neither the credential it rests on nor its user.

static_check.detects: A cached authorization result with a TTL above max_authz_cache_ttl_seconds, or a cache key for an authorization result that does not include the principal.

lens.ask: Is any cached value derived from one caller's permissions readable by another caller?

rules.title: The service is correct without its cache and safe from stampedes
rules.intent: A cache is an optimization; hot keys are protected by coalescing or early refresh.

lens.ask: Does the service stay correct with the cache empty or down, and what protects a hot key from a stampede when it expires?
